title: Existence of a positive solution for a generalized quasilinear Schrodinger equation with asymptotically linear nonlinearity via the Nehari manifold (Theorem 1.1)
author: Xuan Long; Xiang-Dong Fang
work: Positive solutions for generalized quasilinear Schrodinger equations
source_version: Electronic Journal of Differential Equations 2026, No. 19, pp. 1--16; DOI 10.58997/ejde.2026.19; publisher version
difficulty_reason: The counted statement is the paper's main existence theorem, and its written proof (source lines 1086--1114) is short precisely because it is the top of a source-local chain: the difficulty is the chain, which is delivered in full. Because the nonlinearity is only asymptotically linear, the mountain-pass geometry alone cannot produce a nontrivial solution and the fixed-sign Nehari manifold is not a manifold, so the authors work on the Nehari manifold split into two pieces through the auxiliary function and the map n, and the proof must (i) treat the easy cases through Propositions 3.14 and 3.15, where Ekeland variational principle is legitimised on the constrained set by the lemma preventing the limiting point from reaching the boundary (line 842), and where the concentration-compactness lemma for Palais-Smale sequences together with the norm equivalence turns the weak limit into a strong one (lines 847--850 and 884--895); (ii) in the remaining case, where the barycentric infimum is strictly larger than the limiting level, construct the modified path built from the dilation parameter and the scaling that returns the translated ground state to the Nehari manifold, whose properties are exactly Lemmas 3.16 to 3.20, including the reformulation of hypothesis (A11) as an interval condition and the strict inequality for the path level (lines 1007--1084); and (iii) run a deformation argument on the Nehari manifold to build a continuous map of a ball into its own boundary that is the identity on the boundary, a contradiction of the quoted topological fact (lines 1090--1110), after which sign-definiteness, elliptic regularity and the maximum principle upgrade the critical point to a positive solution (lines 1111--1113). Minimax theory on a Nehari manifold for a non-local quasilinear operator, with concentration compactness and a barycentre argument, is research-level material with no qualifying-exam counterpart, so the unit is graded H3.
